title: Adaptive Human Resource Management under Persistent Constraint: Sustaining the Teaching Workforce in a Rural Private School
text_snippet: Adaptive Human Resource Management under Persistent Constraint: Sustaining the Teaching Workforce in a Rural Private School Rural private schools often face persistent financial scarcity and policy volatility, yet limited attention has been given to how such conditions shape teacher workforce sustainability through organizational processes. This study examines how a rural private school sustains its teaching workforce amid persistent financial constraints and changing educational policies. The qualitative case study approach with an interpretative phenomenological analysis (IPA) was conducted using semi-structured interviews with 14 participants comprizing the Foundation Chairman, Foundation Secretary, principal, and 11 teachers at SMP Cendikia Sukahegar (SMP CS), Cianjur, West Java, Indonesia. The findings identified five interconnected themes emerged: scarcity as a shared organizational condition; policy volatility as organizational discontinuity; HRM reconfiguration around financial scarcity; retention through relational and professional exchange; and collective agency through foundation–principal–teacher collaboration. title: An Interactive E-Module for Expository Writing Skills and Motivation in Elementary Students
text_snippet: An Interactive E-Module for Expository Writing Skills and Motivation in Elementary Students This research and development study aimed to design an interactive e-module based on Flipping Book Publisher to improve expository writing skills and learning motivation among fifth-grade elementary school students. A preliminary needs analysis conducted at an elementary school in Makassar City revealed that most Grade V students struggled with expository writing and perceived conventional, teacher-centered instruction as unmotivating, indicating both a skills deficit and an unaddressed motivational gap. The study employed the Four-D model (Define, Design, Develop, Disseminate) with a one-group pretest-posttest design, without a control group, to design, validate, and preliminarily evaluate the e-module. The module integrates six multimedia components grounded in the Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning, constructivism, and self-determination theory. Data were collected from three expert validators, 38 Grade V students, and 15 teachers using validation sheets, student and teacher response questionnaires, a writing skills test, and a motivation questionnaire. title: Developing a Rational–Reflective Counseling Model Integrating Peace Values to Enhance School Counselors' Professional Competence in Promoting Digital-Friendly Schools
text_snippet: Developing a Rational–Reflective Counseling Model Integrating Peace Values to Enhance School Counselors' Professional Competence in Promoting Digital-Friendly Schools The increasing prevalence of cyberbullying in digital learning environments requires school counselors to adopt counseling approaches that are both evidence-based and culturally responsive. However, integrating psychological interventions with local wisdom remains a challenge in school counseling practice. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a Rational–Reflective Counseling Model Integrating Peace Values to enhance school counselors' professional competence in promoting digitally friendly schools. A Research and Development (R&D) design adapted from Borg and Gall was employed through three phases: pre-development, development, and post-development. Sixteen senior high school counselors in Central Java, Indonesia, were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using needs assessment and professional competence questionnaires, expert validation sheets, observation checklists, and semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Aiken's V, Cronbach's alpha, paired-samples t-test, and normalized gain (N-gain) in Jamovi, while qualitative data were analyzed using thematic analysis. title: The Implications of School Culture Management for Fostering Students’ Moderate Attitudes
text_snippet: The Implications of School Culture Management for Fostering Students’ Moderate Attitudes This study aims to analyze and study the implications of the implementation of school culture management in strengthening the moderate attitudes of elementary school students. This study uses a qualitative method with a case study approach conducted at State Elementary School 03 Tanjung, Jepara Regency. Informants from this study consisted of the Principal, Class Teachers, Religion Teachers and students who were selected purposively according to the research data needs. Data collection techniques were carried out through interviews, observations, and documentation, while data analysis was carried out interactively through the stages of data reduction, data presentation, and drawing conclusions. The results of the study indicate that the implementation of school culture management has significant implications in strengthening students' moderate attitudes. title: Bibliometric Mapping of Vocational Teacher Adaptation in the Era of Industry 4.0: An Analysis of 315 Scopus Documents (2016–2026)
text_snippet: Bibliometric Mapping of Vocational Teacher Adaptation in the Era of Industry 4.0: An Analysis of 315 Scopus Documents (2016–2026) Background of study: The advance of Industry 4.0, artificial intelligence (AI), and digital transformation has reshaped Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) and requires vocational teachers to develop adaptive capacities aligned with twenty-first-century learning demands, yet the knowledge structure and research direction in this area have not been comprehensively mapped. Aims and scope of paper: This study analyzes the intellectual structure, developmental trends, and thematic clusters of research on vocational teacher adaptation. Methods: A total of 315 Scopus-indexed documents, exported in RIS format on 19 July 2026, were examined through performance analysis and science mapping using VOSviewer version 1.6.18. Result: Publication output increased sharply, with more than half of the documents (163 publications) issued in 2025–2026. China, Indonesia, and Malaysia were the most productive countries, although international collaboration remained relatively low at 18.4%. title: Usability and User Experience Evaluation of the SEHATI LMS for Triple Burden of Malnutrition Education among Adolescents
text_snippet: Usability and User Experience Evaluation of the SEHATI LMS for Triple Burden of Malnutrition Education among Adolescents Background of study: Indonesian adolescents face a triple burden of malnutrition (TBM), yet engaging digital media for TBM education remain limited. SEHATI is a learning management system (LMS) delivering TBM education through a flipped classroom approach using comics, games, videos, and posters. Aims and scope of paper: This study evaluated the usability, user experience (UX), specific features, and flipped classroom learning implementation of the SEHATI LMS among adolescents. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study involved 30 junior high school students (aged 13–14 years; 50% male) who completed a modified System Usability Scale (SUS), the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ), a 32-item feature evaluation, a five-item flipped classroom evaluation, and five open-ended questions. Result: The mean SUS score was 73 ± 10.8 (Good), with 70% of participants rating the system Good or Excellent. All six UEQ dimensions were rated positively; Stimulation was highest (83.3% Excellent), and the overall mean scale score was 1.68. title: Item Analysis of Mathematical Critical Thinking Skills Using the Rasch Model in Elementary School Students
text_snippet: Item Analysis of Mathematical Critical Thinking Skills Using the Rasch Model in Elementary School Students The validity and reliability of educational assessment instruments are fundamental prerequisites for accurate measurement of student competencies. This study evaluates the psychometric quality of a 12-item mathematical critical thinking test grounded in the Facione framework, encompassing Interpretation, Analysis, Inference, and Evaluation, administered to 49 Grade V elementary school students (n = 49) using the Rasch measurement model via Winsteps software. Four psychometric dimensions were assessed simultaneously: (1) construct validity through item fit statistics (Outfit MNSQ, Outfit ZSTD, Pt Measure Corr); (2) internal consistency and reliability (KR-20, Person and Item Reliability, Separation Indices); (3) item discrimination (Pt Measure Corr classification); and (4) item difficulty hierarchy (logit scale measures and Wright Person–Item Map). Results show that 10 of 12 items (83.3%) met Rasch fit criteria, yielding construct-valid measures for all four critical thinking indicators. title: The Effect of Employment Prospects, Parental Socioeconomic Status, and Career Motivation on Students’ Higher Education Intentions
text_snippet: The Effect of Employment Prospects, Parental Socioeconomic Status, and Career Motivation on Students’ Higher Education Intentions Higher education intentions play a crucial role in preparing students to navigate the digital transformation and the demands of 21st-century industry. This quantitative explanatory study was employed to examine the effects of employment prospects, parental socioeconomic status, and career motivation on the higher education intentions of students at the Indonesian Embassy School in Riyadh. A saturated sampling technique was applied, involving all 53 regular and distance learning senior high school students enrolled during the second semester of the 2025/2026 academic year. Primary data were collected through a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire administered via Google Forms. The data were analyzed using inferential statistical techniques with SPSS version 23. The findings indicate that employment prospects, parental socioeconomic status, and career motivation simultaneously exert a significant effect on students' higher education intentions. title: Discourse on Development and Marginalization of Local Communities: A Critical Discourse Analysis of National Strategic Projects in Indonesia
text_snippet: Discourse on Development and Marginalization of Local Communities: A Critical Discourse Analysis of National Strategic Projects in Indonesia This study examines how development discourse is constructed, disseminated, and embedded in relations of power and the marginalization of local communities within Indonesia’s National Strategic Projects. Using Norman Fairclough’s Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA), the study adopts a qualitative critical approach encompassing three dimensions: textual analysis, discursive practice, and social practice. The data consist of online news articles, government statements, policy documents, and related digital content concerning national strategic projects, collected through documentation and literature study and analyzed through textual, discursive-practice, and social-practice analysis. The findings reveal that, at the textual level, national strategic projects development is constructed through positive diction, progressive metaphors, technocratic terminology, and euphemistic expressions that legitimize development while obscuring social conflicts, land disputes, and the experiences of affected communities. title: The Integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the Development of Javanese Language Instructional Material: An Analysis of Teachers’ Strategies, Challenges, and Practices
text_snippet: The Integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the Development of Javanese Language Instructional Material: An Analysis of Teachers’ Strategies, Challenges, and Practices The presence and rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has expanded its potential use in education and generated pedagogical and ethical challenges in education all at once, particularly in locality-based learning. Despite continuous development of studies on AI in education, the studies exploring how teacher utilizes AI to develop teaching material maintaining local language and culture characteristics are still limited. This research is intended to explore Javanese language teachers’ perspective on their strategies, challenges, and practices in utilizing AI to design instructional materials. Using qualitative method supporting with in-depth interview with seven Javanese language teachers experienced in using AI in instructional material design. Data analysis revealed three main findings. First, teachers utilized AI as a means of identifying students’ needs and materials, enhancing content, and drafting early instructional material. title: Digital Maestros: Dissecting the Seven Crucial Dimensions of Digital Literacy Competencies for Vocational Teachers' Digital Creativity
text_snippet: Digital Maestros: Dissecting the Seven Crucial Dimensions of Digital Literacy Competencies for Vocational Teachers' Digital Creativity Digital transformation in vocational education requires a reconceptualization of teacher competencies, but a comprehensive understanding of digital creativity literacy competencies is still limited. This study aims to analyze the conceptualization of digital creativity literacy competencies in the context of vocational education, identify the main dimensions that shape them, and explore effective development models to improve these competencies in vocational teachers. A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted on 12 recent publications (2023-2025) from the Scopus database using the PRISMA approach with strict inclusion and exclusion criteria. The results of the analysis reveal the evolution of the concept from a technocentric understanding to a multidimensional construct that integrates technical, creative, and pedagogical aspects. Seven competency dimensions were identified, including technical/operational (92%), creative/production (100%), pedagogical (100%), critical/evaluative (83%), social/collaborative (75%), ethical/responsibility (67%), and cultural/contextual (58%), which vary significantly between vocational fields (engineering, business, health). title: Effectiveness of Guided Inquiry Student Worksheet Supplemented with Chemistry Mystery Box Improving Students’ Problem-Solving Skills Regarding Reaction Rate Factors Material
text_snippet: Effectiveness of Guided Inquiry Student Worksheet Supplemented with Chemistry Mystery Box Improving Students’ Problem-Solving Skills Regarding Reaction Rate Factors Material Problem-solving skills are one of the key competencies that need to be developed in chemistry education. However, students’ proficiency in this area remains relatively low, particularly regarding the factors that influence reaction rates. Therefore, this study aims to analyze the effectiveness of guided inquiry-based learning activities supplemented with the Chemistry Mystery Box media in improving students’ problem-solving skills. This study employed a One-Group Pretest-Posttest design involving 31 11th-grade students at a senior high school in Sidoarjo Regency. The research instrument consisted of a problem-solving skills test administered before and after instruction. The data obtained were analyzed using descriptive statistics, the N-Gain test, the normality test, and the Wilcoxon test. The results showed that students’ average scores increased from the pretest to the posttest, with an average N-Gain score of 0.7207 which falls into the high category and N-Gain scores for each indicator of 0.661, 0.703, 0.768, 0.721, and 0.757, respectively, falling into the moderate and high categories. title: From Technology-Driven Engagement to Learning Effectiveness: A Systematic Literature Review of Mobile Learning in Higher Education
text_snippet: From Technology-Driven Engagement to Learning Effectiveness: A Systematic Literature Review of Mobile Learning in Higher Education This study aims to explore student interest, satisfaction, effectiveness, and the supporting factors and challenges of mobile learning in higher education. Using the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method with the PRISMA strategy, it analyzes articles published between 2015-2025 from Scopus, Science Direct, Taylor and Francis, and Eric. The keywords included “mobile learning”, “m-learning”, “android-based”, and “higher education”. Out of 1,919 articles found, 42 met the inclusion and exclusion criteria for analysis. Findings reveal that student interest in mobile learning grows with technological advancements. Students are generally satisfied with the user-friendly interface, and most find m-learning effective for education. Key success factors include engaging and relevant content design. However, challenges such as data security, privacy, and integration into formal curricula persist. Further research is needed to examine the availability of supportive technology in educational institutions to enhance mobile learning experiences.

title: Measuring the Four Cognitive Strands of Mathematical Proficiency in Primary School: A Systematic Review of Measurement Properties
text_snippet: Measuring the Four Cognitive Strands of Mathematical Proficiency in Primary School: A Systematic Review of Measurement Properties Mathematical proficiency in the primary years comprises four interwoven cognitive strands conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, strategic competence, and adaptive reasoning yet how well existing instruments measure them is unclear. This systematic review examined how these strands are operationalised in primary-school students and appraised the psychometric quality of the instruments used. Following the PRISMA 2020 statement and COSMIN methodology, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for English-language articles published between 2010 and 2026, yielding 40 studies. Conceptual understanding and procedural fluency were assessed far more often than strategic competence and adaptive reasoning; only one study operationalised all four strands, and its factor analysis recovered just two. Structural validity dominated by the Rasch/item-response-theory family was the most frequently reported property, whereas inter-rater reliability, content validity, and measurement invariance were seldom examined, and responsiveness was not established in any study. title: The Effect of The Intensity of Book Deliberation on Students' Learning Motivation in Diniyah Learning
text_snippet: The Effect of The Intensity of Book Deliberation on Students' Learning Motivation in Diniyah Learning The integration of formal and classical (salaf) education curricula in contemporary Islamic boarding schools often places excessive cognitive burden on students, leading to a decline in their intrinsic motivation to study the yellow books as the primary source of classical Islamic knowledge. Based on Self-Determination Theory, this study aims to empirically test the significance of the intensity of yellow book discussions on students' learning motivation at the diniyah education level at the Islamic Boarding School. This study uses a quantitative correlational design with an ex post facto approach. Data collection was conducted through a validated five-point Likert scale questionnaire distributed to 163 respondents consisting of Marhalah Ula (n = 85) and Marhalah Wustho (n = 78) students, selected using proportionate stratified random sampling technique to ensure sample representativeness at both levels. Data analysis was conducted through simple linear regression and Pearson correlation tests. title: Indonesian Primary School Teachers’ Perceptions of STEMPreneur for Supporting Computational Thinking in Science Learning
text_snippet: Indonesian Primary School Teachers’ Perceptions of STEMPreneur for Supporting Computational Thinking in Science Learning The increasing emphasis on computational thinking (CT) in primary education has encouraged the exploration of innovative pedagogical approaches that integrate scientific inquiry with authentic problem solving. One emerging approach is STEMPreneur, which combines STEM education with entrepreneurial thinking to foster innovation and value creation. This study explored Indonesian primary school teachers' perceptions of STEMPreneur for promoting computational thinking in Primary Science (IPAS) learning. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed involving 50 primary school teachers from Jakarta and Bekasi, followed by semi-structured interviews with five purposively selected participants. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, while qualitative data were examined through thematic analysis. The findings revealed that teachers perceived STEMPreneur as a relevant and pedagogically valuable approach that supports the development of decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, algorithmic thinking, and evaluation. title: Integration of 21st Century Skills (4C) in Extracurricular Robotics
text_snippet: Integration of 21st Century Skills (4C) in Extracurricular Robotics This study examines how 21st-century skills (4C) are internalized within a post-revitalization robotics extracurricular ecosystem at a public senior high school in East Java. Using a qualitative case study, data were obtained from eight purposively selected informants (one principal, one supervising teacher, and six students) through semi-structured interviews, participant observation, and document analysis. Data were analyzed iteratively through organizing, memoing, initial coding, category development, cross-source comparison, and thematic consolidation. Credibility was strengthened through method and source triangulation and member checking. The findings identify three interrelated processes. First, critical thinking and creativity developed through diagnosing technical failures, testing alternatives, revising designs, and producing context-responsive technologies such as ACF TEHNO and RATA OBAMA. Second, collaboration and communication developed through role specialization, peer tutoring, egalitarian discussion, and technology-literacy outreach. title: Rethinking Cybersecurity Literacy for Non-IT Teachers: Frameworks, Pedagogical Challenges, and Future Directions
text_snippet: Rethinking Cybersecurity Literacy for Non-IT Teachers: Frameworks, Pedagogical Challenges, and Future Directions Digital threats in schools have grown faster than most non-IT teachers' capacity to respond, yet cybersecurity literacy frameworks remain built around technical proficiency rather than classroom practice. This systematic literature review and narrative analysis (SLNA) examines how cybersecurity competency models for non-IT teachers have evolved between 2015 and 2025, and why implementation continues to lag behind framework design. Guided by the PICOS and PRISMA 2020 protocols, the review screened 313 records from Scopus and Consensus AI, retaining 39 studies after full-text eligibility assessment. Bibliometric and thematic analysis traced three research phases (foundation, expansion, consolidation), five dominant thematic clusters, and clear geographic asymmetries, with Europe and North America producing 74.3% of the literature. Findings show that resource-constrained contexts, despite fewer studies, generated a higher innovation index (95%) than well-resourced settings (70%), driven by culturally grounded, low-tech, and community-based solutions. title: Mapping Madurese Cultural Heritage for Secondary Science Education: An Ethnopedagogical Study in Sumenep, Indonesia
text_snippet: Mapping Madurese Cultural Heritage for Secondary Science Education: An Ethnopedagogical Study in Sumenep, Indonesia Science education increasingly requires contextual approaches that connect scientific concepts with students’ cultural experiences. However, local cultural knowledge is often underutilized as an educational resource, particularly in regions with rich cultural diversity such as Sumenep, Indonesia. Madurese cultural traditions contain various forms of ecological, technological, and social knowledge that remain insufficiently explored within science education. This study aims to identify Madurese cultural traditions in Sumenep and analyze their potential contribution to secondary science education through an ethnopedagogical perspective. The study focuses on mapping cultural practices, educational values, science-related knowledge, and potential learning approaches without claiming classroom effectiveness. A qualitative descriptive design was employed involving cultural exploration through semi-structured interviews, observations, and document analysis. Ten cultural informants were selected using purposive and snowball sampling techniques. Data were analyzed through thematic analysis to identify cultural themes, science-related phenomena, and preliminary ethnopedagogical connections.

title: Evaluating Computer-Based Testing System Success Using the DeLone and McLean Model among Cadets at an Indonesian Aviation Higher Education Institution
text_snippet: Evaluating Computer-Based Testing System Success Using the DeLone and McLean Model among Cadets at an Indonesian Aviation Higher Education Institution The rapid adoption of Computer-Based Testing (CBT) in higher education requires an evaluation framework to determine whether the implemented system successfully provides benefits for users. This study aims to evaluate the success of CBT implementation among cadets of a higher education institution in Indonesia using the DeLone and McLean Information Systems Success Model. A quantitative explanatory approach was employed involving 108 cadets who had experience using the CBT system. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 3.2.9. The evaluation consisted of measurement model assessment and structural model testing using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples. The results indicate that information quality significantly influences user satisfaction (β = 0.399, p = 0.001), and service quality significantly influences user satisfaction (β = 0.298, p = 0.011). However, system quality does not significantly influence user satisfaction (β = 0.225, p = 0.055). title: Development of ISLE-Based Science E-Modules in Improving Disaster Mitigation Literacy of High School Students in Tectonic Prone Areas
text_snippet: Development of ISLE-Based Science E-Modules in Improving Disaster Mitigation Literacy of High School Students in Tectonic Prone Areas Aceh Province is geologically flanked by two active tectonic systems: the Sunda Megathrust subduction zone and the Sumatra Fault, making disaster mitigation literacy a crucial survival skill for high school students. However, conventional science learning is still dominated by textual memorization and lacks relevance to the context of local disasters, which has an impact on students' weak practical mitigation skills. This research aims to design, develop, and test the effectiveness of science e-modules based on the Investigative Science Learning Environment (ISLE) model through an interactive application called Si-AGAM (Aceh Earthquake & Mitigation Investigative Science) to improve students' disaster mitigation literacy. Using a Research and Development (R&D) approach with the ADDIE framework, this research was carried out at SMAN 1 Banda Aceh. The data collection instruments included expert validation sheets, teacher and student practicality questionnaires, and 15 multiple-choice questions to measure mitigation literacy. title: Implementation of The Critical Thinking Skills Measurement Instrument Integrated with the Critical and Creative Thinking in Research-Based Learning Model
text_snippet: Implementation of The Critical Thinking Skills Measurement Instrument Integrated with the Critical and Creative Thinking in Research-Based Learning Model This study addresses the limited availability of critical thinking assessment instruments that comprehensively measure university students' competencies in higher education. Existing FRISCO-based instruments are constrained by suboptimal internal consistency, a predominant focus on cognitive dimensions, limited assessment of critical thinking dispositions, and potential subjectivity arising from inconsistent interpretation of assessment criteria. To overcome these limitations, the Critical Thinking Skills Measurement Instrument (CTSMI) integrated with the Critical and Creative Thinking Research-based Learning (CCTRbL) model was developed. This study aimed to examine the validity, effectiveness, implementation fidelity, and user acceptability of the integrated CTSMI. A mixed-methods approach combining a pre-experimental design and Collaborative Action Research (CAR) was employed, involving four lecturers and a hundred undergraduate students. title: Mapping Methodological Approaches to Critical Digital Literacy Among TVET Instructors: A Scoping Review
text_snippet: Mapping Methodological Approaches to Critical Digital Literacy Among TVET Instructors: A Scoping Review Digital competence frameworks for teachers have proliferated, but whether their critical, reflective dimension has been examined among technical and vocational education and training (TVET) instructors remains uncharacterized. This scoping review characterized the methodological approaches, conceptual operationalizations, and evidence gaps in peer-reviewed research on critical digital literacy (CDL) among TVET instructors. Following Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and reported per PRISMA-ScR, Scopus was searched on 3 July 2026 using a Population-Concept-Context strategy, restricted to English-language, peer-reviewed literature from 2013–2026. Eligible sources were charted against a framework combining bibliographic, PCC, and methodological data items. Eighty sources met the eligibility criteria. Results included sources concentrated in Western, Northern, and Southern Europe (30.0%) and Southeast Asia (27.5%, including Indonesia at 22.5%), with smaller shares from East Asia, Eastern Europe/Central Asia, and other regions. title: Beyond Traditional Management: Transforming Islamic Boarding School Management through Orange Data Mining
text_snippet: Beyond Traditional Management: Transforming Islamic Boarding School Management through Orange Data Mining The management of Indonesian Islamic boarding schools (pesantren) generally remains rooted in traditional administrative practices with limited use of data-driven decision-making, which constrains strategic development and organizational effectiveness. Aims and scope of paper: This study aims to develop a transformative management model for a pesantren in Blitar by integrating data mining techniques with quantitative strategic planning to enhance institutional performance and responsiveness to stakeholder needs. Methods: The research involved multiple stakeholders, including administrators, students, parents, alumni, and community members. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered via an online platform and analyzed using data mining software. The analytical process included data cleaning, normalization, text preprocessing, and the application of clustering, classification, and association rule techniques to identify patterns, themes, and sentiments. Strategic alternatives were then prioritized using a quantitative strategic planning approach based on weighted internal and external factors. title: Teacher Readiness for Implementing the Deep Learning Approach in Elementary School Education in the Society 5.0 Era
text_snippet: Teacher Readiness for Implementing the Deep Learning Approach in Elementary School Education in the Society 5.0 Era This study aims to analyze the readiness of elementary school teachers to implement deep learning in the Digital 5.0 era. The study used a mixed methods approach with a sequential explanatory design. The study subjects consisted of 364 elementary school teachers in Ponorogo Regency, Indonesia. The sample was selected using simple random sampling. Data were collected through questionnaires, interviews, observations, and documentation. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, while qualitative data were analyzed through source triangulation. The results showed that teacher readiness in implementing deep learning tended to be in the moderate category. Teachers' pedagogical and social competencies were in the moderate category, while their technological and professional competencies were in the high category. Supporting factors for deep learning implementation included support from school leaders, collaboration between teachers, teacher motivation to innovate, professional training, and the use of learning technology. title: Development of a Citizen Science Project-Based Teaching Module to Improve Creative Thinking and Collaboration Skills on Ecology and Biodiversity Materials
text_snippet: Development of a Citizen Science Project-Based Teaching Module to Improve Creative Thinking and Collaboration Skills on Ecology and Biodiversity Materials Creative thinking and collaboration skills are important 21st-century competencies that need to be developed through science learning. However, observations in junior high schools in West Pasaman, Indonesia show that students' creative thinking skills are still low with an average of 47.875%, while collaboration skills have not developed optimally because there are still passive students in discussion and group work activities. This study aims to produce a valid, practical, and effective Citizen Science Project-based teaching module to improve students' creative thinking and collaboration skills in Ecology and Biodiversity material. title: The Relationship between TikTok and YouTube Use and Teaching Creativity of Economics Teachers in Pontianak City, Indonesia
text_snippet: The Relationship between TikTok and YouTube Use and Teaching Creativity of Economics Teachers in Pontianak City, Indonesia The rise of video-based social media, particularly TikTok and YouTube, has opened new avenues for teachers to enhance their instructional creativity, yet empirical evidence within secondary-level economics education remains limited. This study examined the effect of TikTok application use and YouTube learning media on the teaching creativity of economics teachers in senior high schools across Pontianak City, both partially and simultaneously. A quantitative correlational survey design was employed. Data were collected through an online five-point Likert questionnaire from 423 students (214 female, 209 male) across seven senior high schools in Pontianak, capturing their perceptions of teachers' TikTok and YouTube use and teaching creativity. Data were analyzed using item validity and Cronbach's Alpha reliability testing, classical assumption tests, and multiple linear regression with heteroscedasticity-consistent (HC3) robust standard errors. title: The Influence of MYOB Accounting Software Implementation, Learning Motivation, and Learning Interest on Vocational Students’ Competency Improvement in Computer Accounting Competency
text_snippet: The Influence of MYOB Accounting Software Implementation, Learning Motivation, and Learning Interest on Vocational Students’ Competency Improvement in Computer Accounting Competency This study examined the influence of MYOB Accounting Software implementation, learning motivation, and learning interest on students’ competency improvement in Computer Accounting subjects at SMKN 1 Penajam Paser Utara. The study employed a quantitative approach using explanatory research design. Data were collected through questionnaires, tests, observations, and documentation involving 98 vocational students from the Accounting and Institutional Finance Department. Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression with the assistance of Stata MP 17 software. The findings revealed that partially MYOB Accounting Software implementation, learning motivation, and learning interest did not significantly influence students’ competency improvement, with significance values of 0.6148, 0.4867, and 0.5535 respectively (p > 0.05). Simultaneously, the three variables also did not significantly affect competency improvement (Prob > F = 0.6879). title: Early Childhood Education Teachers' Perception of the Implementation of the Collaborative Reflection Model in Character Education
text_snippet: Early Childhood Education Teachers' Perception of the Implementation of the Collaborative Reflection Model in Character Education Early childhood character education often still relies on passive one-way instruction, even though this approach has proven to be less effective in instilling moral values than direct experience and interaction. This study aims to explore the perception of early childhood education teachers towards the implementation of the collaborative reflection model in character education, especially regarding relevance, feasibility, obstacles, and support needs in daily pedagogical practice. The study used a qualitative descriptive case study design involving educators at a daycare in Cileungsi, Bogor Regency, selected through purposive criterion sampling, with data collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews, pre- and post-observation binary questionnaires, and thetically analyzed field notes. The results showed that teachers' perceptions underwent a significant transformation, from technical concerns in the pre-observation phase regarding time constraints and difficulties in conditioning children, to full approval of the feasibility of the model after witnessing hands-on practice modeling in the classroom. title: Educational Media for Enhancing Sexual Awareness in Children with Intellectual Disabilities: A Systematic Literature Review and Bibliometric Analysis
text_snippet: Educational Media for Enhancing Sexual Awareness in Children with Intellectual Disabilities: A Systematic Literature Review and Bibliometric Analysis This study aims to analyze global publication trends and synthesize the mapping of design components, focus, and key findings from studies on the development of educational media based on sexual awareness for children with intellectual disabilities. The study was conducted through a systematic literature review from 2010–2026 using a qualitative descriptive approach with bibliometric and meta-aggregation analyses. The results indicate that only a few studies specifically address the development of educational media for children with intellectual disabilities and sexual awareness. Most studies focus on the use of innovative media such as Augmented Reality (AR), and empirically, learner-centered and play-based approaches have demonstrated higher effectiveness in children’s engagement and learning outcomes. The limitations identified in the reviewed literature indicate that the educational media currently developed generally still rely on broad validation instruments rather than those specifically designed according to children’s developmental stages and socio-cultural contexts. text_snippet: Improving Phase C Students’ Persuasive Text Comprehension through DRTA Assisted by Advertisement Card Media This study was conducted to examine the effectiveness of the Directed Reading Thinking Activity (DRTA) model supported by advertisement card media in improving persuasive text reading comprehension skills among Phase C elementary school students. This study employed a quantitative approach using a pre-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design. The participants consisted of 15 fifth-grade elementary school students. Data were collected through multiple-choice reading comprehension tests administered before and after the treatment. The results indicated a statistically significant improvement in students’ reading comprehension skills following the implementation of the DRTA model assisted by advertisement card media. title: The Integration of Ahmad Dahlan’s Teachings Through Psychoeducation-Based Virtual Reality to Enhance Students’ Peace
text_snippet: The Integration of Ahmad Dahlan’s Teachings Through Psychoeducation-Based Virtual Reality to Enhance Students’ Peace This study aims to test the effectiveness of virtual reality (VR)-based psychoeducation based on the teachings of K.H. Ahmad Dahlan in improving the calmness of vocational high school students. The study used a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental method through a non-equivalent control group pretest-posttest design. The study participants consisted of 16 11th-grade students identified as having low levels of comfort and were divided into an experimental group and a control group. The experimental group received five sessions of VR-assisted psychoeducation that integrated the spiritual-humanistic values of K.H. Ahmad Dahlan, while the control group received treatment as usual. Data were collected using a validated Peace Scale consisting of 26 items covering aspects of self-harmony, social harmony, and environmental harmony. The instrument demonstrated good reliability with a Cronbach's Alpha coefficient of 0.849. Data analysis was performed using the Mann–Whitney U test to test for differences between groups. title: Confronting Gender-Based Violence in Nigerian Higher Institutions: Creating Safe and Inclusive Campuses as an Imperative for Educational Transformation
text_snippet: Confronting Gender-Based Violence in Nigerian Higher Institutions: Creating Safe and Inclusive Campuses as an Imperative for Educational Transformation Gender-based violence (GBV) could be describes as a pervasive issue that remains systematically under addressed and under-reported within the Nigerian higher education system. This menace, no doubt, is exacting severe consequences on student wellbeing, academic performance, institutional reputation, and national human capital development. This paper examines the nature, prevalence, drivers, and multi-dimensional implications of GBV across Nigerian tertiary institutions and used Feminist Theory, particularly gender power theory as articulated by Connell (2005)., Institutional Theory (DiMaggio & Powell, 1983) and Communication Theory, particularly Habermas's (1984) theory of communicative action, as theoretical frameworks. Drawing on empirical studies, the theoretical frameworks, and existing legal and policy instruments, the paper identifies sexual harassment, peer-based violence, and institutional silence as dominant manifestations of GBV, while locating their persistence in entrenched patriarchal norms, asymmetrical power relations, rapid institutional growth outpacing governance capacity, and chronically weak enforcement mechanisms. title: Development of Jenga Collaboration with Combo Cards Learning Media on Ecosystem Material for Grade VII Students
text_snippet: Development of Jenga Collaboration with Combo Cards Learning Media on Ecosystem Material for Grade VII Students The low level of student engagement and collaboration in group-based science learning, particularly on the abstract topic of ecosystems, underlies this study. Preliminary observations at three junior high schools in Majenang District, Indonesia revealed limited use of interactive learning media that supports collaboration among students, consistent with data showing that 75% of students had not reached the Minimum Mastery Criteria (MMC) on ecosystem material. This study aims to develop the Jenga Collaboration with Combo Cards learning media and to examine its feasibility and effectiveness. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using the 4-D model (Define, Design, Develop, Disseminate), limited to the Develop stage. title: The Effectiveness and Implementation of Formative Assessment in Primary Education: A Systematic Literature Review
text_snippet: The Effectiveness and Implementation of Formative Assessment in Primary Education: A Systematic Literature Review Although formative assessment stands as a pillar of high-quality pedagogy, its integration into Indonesian primary education remains hamstrung by persistent systemic hurdles. This systematic literature review (SLR), anchored in the PRISMA protocol, scrutinised 32 high-impact studies published from 2019 to 2024. The study’s core objectives were threefold: (1) to evaluate how specific formative strategies drive student achievement; (2) to map the variables that either facilitate or obstruct successful implementation; and (3) to propose evidence-based benchmarks tailored to the Indonesian context. Findings indicate that well-calibrated formative practices yield a substantial effect size (d = 0.38–0.78) on pupil outcomes, particularly when the feedback loop is immediate, specific, and actionable. Eight standout strategies emerged: exit tickets, Socratic questioning, peer and self-assessment, gamified digital tools, structured observations, mathematical journals, and mini-whiteboards. Despite these advantages, the transition is often stalled by a trifecta of barriers: gaps in teacher competence, heavy administrative overhead, and infrastructure deficits. text_snippet: Developing a Jimdo-Based Ekanaru Learning Platform Using Problem-Based Learning to Support Elementary Students’ Explanatory Writing Skills This study aims to describe the development process and assess the suitability of the Ekanaru learning resource, based on the Jimdo website and using the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model, for teaching writing skills to fifth-grade public elementary school in Indonesia. The study employed the Research and Development (R&D) method using the ADDIE model, which comprises the stages of analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation. Data were collected through observation, interviews, questionnaires, and documentation, and subsequently analyzed using quantitative descriptive techniques, expressed as percentages. The learning resource developed was integrated with the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model on the Jimdo website platform. The validation results showed an average feasibility percentage of 84.14%, categorized as ‘highly suitable’. title: Critical Discourse Analysis of the Forms of Referential Power in Kike Wadatsumi no Koe's Diary
text_snippet: Critical Discourse Analysis of the Forms of Referential Power in Kike Wadatsumi no Koe's Diary This research aims to describe the forms of power discourse through hegemony representations in diary Kike Wadatsumi no Koe . This research uses a critical qualitative approach. Data analysis techniques are done by reading the data source, documenting the research data, and taking notes the research data includes descriptions, interpretations, and explanations according to the CDA Fairclough model. Data validation is using an intense discussion with competent experts, in addition to figure a triangulation used on data sources and triangulation between researchers. Data are collected into 13 corpus data. title: Board Game Development to Improve College Students' Conflict Management
text_snippet: Board Game Development to Improve College Students' Conflict Management The low conflict management skills of students impact psychological aspects and interpersonal relationships. This study aims to develop a learning medium in the form of a board game as a means to improve students' conflict management skills. The method used is Research and Development (R&D) with the ADDIE model, which includes the stages of Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation. In the analysis stage, data were obtained from 316 students, which showed that most were in the category of medium and low conflict management skills. The design stage was carried out by referring to the Thomas-Kilmann model, which includes five conflict management styles. The developed product was then validated by material, media, and service experts using the Aiken index. Next, the board game was implemented in guidance activities with a pretest and posttest design to measure its effectiveness. The results of the study indicate that the developed board game is suitable for use as a learning medium and has the potential to improve students' communication, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills.
